subject: Label and specify a starting value for a parameter

messages.author: ea5016c05fb289b3
messages.subject: Label and specify a starting value for a parameter
parts:
I want to be able to label parameters in this simple mediation model like
below.

model <- "m ~ a*x
          y ~ c_p*x + b*m"

But I also want to set the starting values like below.

model <- "m ~ start(0.5)*x
          y ~ start(0.0)*x + start(0.5)*m"

Is there a way of label parameters and set starting values at the same time?

Thanks.

-Jek

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Label and specify a starting value for a parameter
parts:
You can mention the same parameter twice:
m~a*x + start(0.5)*x
The syntax interpreter should parse this correctly. The tutorials include some examples like this.

To follow-up on this, it may also be worthwhile to double-check with lavannify() or some such to make sure both the label and starting value are correct. I've noticed the parser sometimes doesn't complain about doing things like: m~ start(0.5)*a*x. And apparently for intercepts the label must come after the starting value:

# works
model<-'
F1 =~ start(.7)*X1 + lam1*X1 + X2 + X3 + X4
X1 ~~ start(.49)*X1 + psi1*X1
X2 ~~ X2
X3 ~~ X3
X4 ~~ X4
X1 ~ mu1*1 + start(1)*1
X2 ~ 1
X3 ~ 1
X4 ~ 1
F1 ~~ start(1)*F1 + vF1*F1
'

lavaanify(model)

messages.subject: Re: Label and specify a starting value for a parameter
parts:
On 12/09/2016 08:10 PM, Carl Falk wrote:
> To follow-up on this, it may also be worthwhile to double-check with
> lavannify() or some such to make sure both the label and starting value
> are correct. I've noticed the parser sometimes doesn't complain about
> doing things like: m~ start(0.5)*a*x.

The parser surely could use many more 'checks'. But checks take time,
and there seems to be no limit to the number of scenarios that we should
check for. Checks are also difficult to write, as it is easy to fool
them, or (even worse) to trigger them while the syntax is in fact correct.

For 0.7 (yes, I realize this is a big jump), I do plan to rewrite the
parser from scratch.

Yves.
